core_obligations: Identify the composite (proof line 21317): both pi_S^{-1} and pi_{S,*} = i_S^{-1} are exact functors, so they compute their own derived functors and the map in the statement is the unit of the adjunction on K.
Use that the composite is the identity (proof lines 21317-21319): the composition pi_{S,*} composed with pi_S^{-1} is the identity functor, hence so is its derived version.
Conclude the isomorphism (proof line 21319): a unit of an adjunction whose composite with the counit is the identity is invertible, so K -> R pi_{S,*} pi_S^{-1} K is an isomorphism.
proof_roadmap: Both functors involved are exact, so no derived functors have to be computed.
The composite pi_{S,*} pi_S^{-1} is the identity functor.
Hence the adjunction unit is the identity as well and the displayed map is an isomorphism.
difficulty_reason: The lemma records the cohomological descent along the projection pi_S to the punctual topos: for K in D(S_etale) the unit K -> R pi_{S,*} pi_S^{-1} K is an isomorphism (statement lines 21307-21314). The content is short but genuinely categorical: one must see that pi_S^{-1} and pi_{S,*} = i_S^{-1} are exact, so that the displayed map is an adjunction unit on the derived category, and that their composite is the identity functor, which forces the unit to be invertible (proof lines 21317-21319). The claim is H2: a two-step derived-categorical identification with no construction beyond it.
